findings.reason: without a bound (elapsed attempt_started_at, or the pointer's supervisor pid shown dead) a crash inside the section's own window converts into a run that refuses every resume forever, contradicting the plan's north star and §11's landed rule.
findings.text: the rule "when attempt.json names an attempt newer than every receipt, that attempt is in flight ... and the reading refuses" has no exit clause for a launch that died inside the window: nothing in the tree unlinks or rewrites attempt.json except a later launch, and every later launch is refused by this same rule, so a launcher killed between `_prepare_attempt_records` writing attempt.json (dispatch_launch.py:2101-2109) and its worker's record leaves the run permanently unlaunchable with no live worker, which is the exact state §11 landed to stop refusing; the neighbouring abandoned-claim path already bounds the same situation with LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS (resumption.py:385-386), and attempt.json already carries `attempt_started_at` (dispatch_launch.py:2106-2107) to bound it the same way

findings.reason: the deliverable's wording ("passes that attempt number so it does not refuse itself") is the unsafe form, so a case admitting a second door that prepares the same attempt number is needed to tell the exemption's scope apart and changes how the guard is written.
findings.text: the four cases never separate a caller-scoped self-exemption from one keyed on the attempt number, and the two are not equivalent: `claim_next_attempt` exists only on the resume path (resumption.py:1705), so dispatch (dispatch.py:3369) takes no claim and two dispatch doors, or a dispatch beside a resume, can both read the same pointer and prepare the same next attempt; the first writes attempt.json, and a guard that exempts "the attempt number I was asked to prepare" admits the second and re-opens the very window this section closes while every stated case still passes

findings.reason: a change to the reader that names the run's live attempt is a second subsystem with its own risk, and folding it into a node graded on the launch refusal means neither a reviewer nor promotion can close one without asserting the other.
findings.text: one node holds the launch refusal in dispatch_launch.py and, as the same deliverable, a refactor of `_attempt_worker_records`/`_read_record` in reckon/crew/resumption.py consumed by `_live_attempt_number` (:1072) and `_attempt_detail` (:1182), plus a recursive rewrite of the real-home fixture in two test files; the four cases measure only the refusal, and the refactor's sole measure is "the test files importing reckon.crew.resumption add no failure against the base"

findings.reason: the implementer must either keep the enumeration local, which the plan forbids, or widen a shared reader in a way the plan does not specify and its gate does not measure, so the deliverable as written is not implementable.
findings.text: "The receipt enumeration and read go through `_attempt_worker_records` and `_read_record` ... widened to the exit receipt if they do not already read it" cannot carry the done-when's exit-receipt semantics without breaking that reader's contract: `_attempt_worker_records` maps one number to one worker payload (resumption.py:1013-1028) whose consumers read `pid` and `launched_at` (:1072, :1184-1190), while an exit receipt carries `exit_code` and `detail` and no pid (tests/test_a_resumed_placed_run_spawns.py:156-164), and one payload per number cannot represent both "this attempt had a worker" and "this attempt filed an exit"

findings.reason: the window exists and the repair is unchanged, so only a supporting sentence needs correcting, though a reader who sizes the window by the watch will mis-size it.
findings.text: "The startup watch can hold that window open for its whole length" does not match the cited code: `on_spawn` writes the worker record immediately after each spawn and before the startup watch runs out its window (dispatch_launch.py:1704-1714, invoked at :3020-3025), so the watch extends the window by nothing; the window is real but bounded by supervisor startup and placement instead
